passage:
I'm Joseph. In November some boys in my class passed around a photo of Reena tripping on the stairs, with a mean caption. I saw it on my phone and did nothing. I didn't laugh and I didn't share, but I didn't speak either. Reena stayed away from school for two days. When she came back, her eyes were red.
I felt sick. I kept telling myself I hadn't done anything, which was exactly the problem.
So I found her at the library door. "I saw that photo and I stayed quiet. I'm sorry. I should have said something." She looked at me for a moment and said, "Thanks for saying it." I have also told our class teacher what I knew. Next time I'll speak sooner.

qa.q: Where did Joseph find Reena to apologise?
qa.a: Joseph found Reena at the library door.
Joseph realised that saying "I hadn't done anything" was exactly the problem: the silence had let Reena be hurt, and Joseph felt guilty.

qa.q: What could Joseph do next time he sees something like this?
qa.a: Joseph could speak up sooner, saying it isn't okay or telling a teacher, and can keep checking that Reena is alright.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt when she came back to school?
qa.a: She was probably hurt and embarrassed, since her eyes were red, so Joseph's apology may have meant a lot to her.

grounding: A teen who stayed quiet while a classmate was hurt feels guilt, apologises, tells the teacher and resolves to speak sooner.

passage: Monday. On the back stairs, Minakshi saw two seniors jostling Shalini, knocking her bag down, laughing. Minakshi pretended to check her phone and walked the other way. Not her business, she told herself. Thursday. Shalini came to school with her arm in a sling. She'd 'slipped' on the same stairs, she said. Minakshi felt sick all through maths. She knew what 'slipped' probably meant, and she had watched it start. That night she couldn't eat. The following Monday. Minakshi went to the class teacher before assembly and told her everything she had seen, with the day and the time. Ms Rao thanked her, spoke with Shalini and the counsellor that morning, and called in the seniors' parents. At lunch Minakshi found Shalini alone. 'I saw them last week and said nothing. I'm really sorry.' Shalini was quiet, then said, 'You said something now.' Next time, Minakshi promised herself, she would not wait.

qa.q: What was on Shalini's arm on Thursday?
How did Minakshi feel after seeing Shalini's sling?
qa.a: She felt sick with guilt, knowing she had watched the pushing begin and said nothing.

qa.q: What did Minakshi do to act on her guilt?
qa.a: She told the class teacher exactly what she had seen and apologised to Shalini directly.

qa.q: How does Shalini seem to see Minakshi's apology?
qa.a: She is quiet at first, then acknowledges that Minakshi has spoken up now, which seems to matter to her.

grounding: Shows a teen who stayed silent before a classmate got hurt, feeling guilt, then reporting, apologising and resolving to speak sooner.

passage: Sahil, you asked why I made you promise to always speak up. Sit. When I was fourteen, in Shimla, a group of girls in my class kept daring my friend Tara to walk along the edge of the school's back wall. I knew it was dangerous. I watched three days in a row and said nothing, because the ringleader was the most popular girl in school. On the fourth day Tara slipped and broke her ankle. I cried all night. I thought I was the worst friend in the world. The next morning my father said, 'The guilt means your heart is working, Charu. Now use it.' I went to the headmistress and told her about the dares, and she stopped them that same day. Then I went to Tara's house and said sorry. She forgave me, slowly. That's why, Sahil. Speak up on the first day, not the fourth.

qa.q: What did the girls dare Tara to do?
qa.a: To walk along the edge of the school's back wall.

qa.q: What was Charu feeling the night Tara broke her ankle?
qa.a: Charu felt crushing guilt, crying all night, sure of being the worst friend in the world.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Charu's story?
qa.a: The father saying guilt means the heart is working, which led Charu to tell the headmistress and apologise to Tara.

qa.q: How did Tara respond to Charu's apology?
qa.a: She forgave Charu slowly, suggesting the hurt was real but the apology mattered.

grounding: An elder's story of staying silent before a friend got hurt, then using the guilt to report, apologise and resolve to speak sooner.
